stem: An analyst runs a SQL cell in a notebook and it fails because a column name in the SELECT list has a small typo. The analyst wants the fastest way to correct it with a suggested change that can be accepted and run. Which Genie Code capability fits?

choices.text: Full page Genie Code, which opens a separate command center to start a new multi-step project
Genie Migrate, which converts SQL written for other data warehouse dialects into Databricks SQL
Quick Fix, which proposes an automatic correction for a basic error that the analyst can accept and run
Genie Ontology, which adds organization-wide business definitions to the prompt before writing SQL

stem: A notebook cell that reads a table fails with a long error caused by the notebook environment rather than by the SQL text. A simple suggested edit of the statement does not help. Which Genie Code feature should the analyst use to investigate and attempt a repair?

choices.text: Command shortcuts, which let the analyst start a prompt directly inside a notebook cell before running it
Diagnose Error, which analyzes more complex errors, including environment errors, and attempts to fix them
Inline suggestions, which complete the next tokens of code while the analyst is typing a new statement
Quick Fix, because it proposes edits only to the statement text and is meant for environment-level failures

stem: An analyst asks Genie Code in the SQL editor for "monthly revenue per region", but the generated query keeps picking the wrong columns from a table with names like c1 and amt_x. What most improves future suggestions for everyone who uses the table?

choices.text: Renaming the personal notebook so that its title explains the revenue logic to the assistant when it runs
Switching the SQL warehouse type from pro to serverless so that prompts are interpreted with more compute
Pasting the full table data into every prompt so that the model can read the values directly each time
Adding clear descriptions to the table and its columns in Unity Catalog so the assistant gets better metadata

stem: A manager asks whether Genie Code can read tables an analyst has not been granted access to, because the analyst wants help with a query on a finance table. How does Genie Code treat access to data?

choices.text: It is limited to the Unity Catalog permissions of the user, so it cannot reach data that user cannot access
It ignores table permissions for column names but enforces them for row values returned by queries
It reads only tables in the catalog that is the default for the workspace, regardless of the user
It uses a service credential with broad read rights, so it can answer from any table in the metastore

stem: A data analyst writes and debugs SQL in the SQL editor all day and wants an assistant to generate queries from prompts. Another team wants a chat interface for business users to explore dashboards and ask data questions. Which pairing of Genie experiences is correct?

choices.text: Genie Code for the analyst writing SQL, and Genie One for the business users who want a simple chat
Genie Agents for the analyst writing SQL, and Genie Code for the business users asking questions
Genie One for the analyst writing SQL, and Genie Code for the business users exploring dashboards
Genie Code for both groups, because every Genie experience is the same product with one interface

stem: Genie Code generated a long query with several joins and the analyst plans to publish its output in a weekly report right away. What is the right practice?

choices.text: Reject the assistant output and rewrite the query manually, because generated joins cannot be trusted at all
Run it unchanged because generated code is always validated against the table schema before it is shown
Run it in production first and compare the report to last week afterwards, to avoid delaying publication
Review the logic and test the results on a sample before publishing, since the assistant can make mistakes

stem: An analyst is typing a new SELECT statement in the SQL editor and wants suggestions for the next column names and clauses to appear as they type, without opening a chat. Which Genie Code capability does this?

choices.text: Diagnose Error, which waits for a failed run before offering any text
Chat with Genie Code, which requires a written question in the chat pane
Inline suggestions and autocomplete, which offer AI-based completions while the analyst writes code
Searched documentation, which cites a documentation page for a conceptual question

stem: A workspace has Genie Code and many AI/BI Genie spaces. A data analyst needs to debug a failing JOIN in a notebook. Which choice is the best tool?

choices.text: The query history page, because it fixes failed statements after sorting them by user
Genie Code in the notebook, because it works with the code and its errors
A Genie space, because it exposes a chat that rewrites notebook cells in place
A scheduled alert, because it can be set to rewrite the failing JOIN when it triggers

stem: An analyst opens the SQL editor and runs a query against Unity Catalog tables. What role does the SQL warehouse play in this execution?

choices.text: It defines which users may see each column, replacing the privileges set in Unity Catalog
It is the compute resource that executes the query, while the data stays in the governed tables
It converts the SQL text into a dashboard automatically when the query returns an aggregate result
It stores the table data files and enforces the table schema, so the query reads only from the warehouse

stem: An analyst runs a query in the SQL editor and sees that the selected warehouse is stopped. The analyst has permission to use it. What happens?

choices.text: The query runs on the SQL editor's own local engine until the warehouse is restarted manually
The query is queued on another running warehouse that the workspace chooses at random
The warehouse starts automatically and runs the query once it is up, after a short startup delay
The query fails immediately and an administrator must start the warehouse before any query can run

stem: On a serverless SQL warehouse, one heavy monthly report query is slow while the warehouse is otherwise idle. The query profile shows the query spilling to disk, and no other queries are queued. Which change addresses this?

choices.text: Increase the cluster size of the warehouse, which gives each cluster more memory and compute for the query
Increase the maximum number of clusters, so that autoscaling adds more clusters for the report query
Switch the warehouse to a classic type, which keeps intermediate results in memory instead of on disk
Add a second warehouse and send the same report query to both so that the faster result is used

stem: On a pro SQL warehouse, many analysts run queries at 9 a.m. and some wait in a queue, although each individual query runs fast once it starts. Which change addresses the symptom?

choices.text: Move the queries into a materialized view so the warehouse no longer needs to run them
Disable Photon, because it limits how many queries can be admitted at the same time
Increase only the cluster size, because bigger clusters allow more queries to run in parallel
Increase the maximum number of clusters so autoscaling can add clusters for the concurrent queries

stem: A new analyst can see tables in Catalog Explorer and has SELECT on them, but the SQL warehouse is not available when running queries. Which additional access is needed?

choices.text: Account admin rights, since every query needs an administrator-level role
Ownership of the catalog, because warehouses are available only to catalog owners
Can view on the SQL warehouse, which lets the analyst run queries but not see history
Can use on the SQL warehouse, which lets the analyst run queries on that compute

stem: An analyst needs to join a Delta table of orders in Unity Catalog with a customers table that lives in an operational PostgreSQL database. The analyst wants to query it in place, governed by Unity Catalog, without copying the data first. What is the approach?

choices.text: Create a connection and a foreign catalog for PostgreSQL, then join its tables with the Delta table in one query
Create a share with Delta Sharing so that PostgreSQL appears as a recipient catalog in the workspace
Export the PostgreSQL table to CSV and upload it through the workspace UI before every query
Convert the Delta table to PostgreSQL and run the join inside the remote database only

stem: An analyst queries a foreign table in a PostgreSQL foreign catalog with `CAST(order_total AS numeric(12,2))`, a type name from PostgreSQL, and the query is rejected. What should the analyst change?

choices.text: Add an OPTIMIZE statement before the query so that the remote column is converted to a Delta type
Ask an administrator to grant MODIFY on the foreign table so that casts to remote types are allowed
Use Spark data types such as `DECIMAL(12,2)`, because Databricks maps them to the remote types
Create the foreign catalog again on a pro warehouse so that PostgreSQL type names are accepted

stem: A data engineer will set up query federation so analysts can query an Oracle database from Databricks SQL. Which order of setup steps is correct?

choices.text: Grant privileges to the analysts, then create the connection, then create the foreign catalog
Create the connection, then create a foreign catalog from it, then grant privileges, then run queries
Create an external location, then a storage credential, then ingest the tables with a pipeline
Create a foreign catalog, then create the connection, then grant privileges, then run queries

stem: An analyst opens Catalog Explorer for a foreign catalog that someone else created and wants to know which external database it mirrors and which stored credentials it uses. What does Catalog Explorer show?

choices.text: Only the name of the foreign catalog, as connection details are hidden from every user including the owner
The usual catalog details plus the connection it uses and the external database it mirrors
A full copy of the external database schema stored as Delta tables inside the foreign catalog
The plain-text username and password of the connection, so that analysts can open their own client

stem: A dashboard shows a daily summary of a large PostgreSQL orders table through a foreign catalog. Every refresh by many viewers runs the same heavy federated aggregation and loads the production database. The team does not want to build an ingestion pipeline. What reduces the load?

choices.text: Create a materialized view over the foreign table so the summary is stored and refreshed, not recomputed
Give each viewer a dedicated warehouse so that the federated aggregation is split across the viewers
Convert the foreign catalog to a managed catalog so the table becomes writable and indexed locally
Create a standard view over the foreign table, which stores the result of the first query for later viewers

stem: An analyst creates a materialized view of employee records for a report. The salary column must be visible only to the hr_team account group, and everyone else with access to the view must get NULL. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Run the materialized view on a classic warehouse, because classic warehouses hide columns from non-admin users
Refresh the materialized view separately for each group, so each group reads its own stored copy of the report
Create the materialized view as temporary so that it applies only to the analyst who created it
Apply a column mask when creating the materialized view, so the salary value depends on the group of the querying user

stem: An analyst created a streaming table from files in a volume. Twenty new files arrived while a REFRESH of the table was running, and the analyst does not see their rows afterwards. What explains it?

choices.text: The refresh failed silently, and the table must be dropped and recreated before any later file is read
Streaming tables read only files that existed when the table was created, so later files never appear
Only data that arrived before the refresh started is processed, and the new files are picked up by the next refresh
The files must first be registered in a materialized view, which then pushes the rows into the streaming table

stem: A table holds customer emails. Auditors must see full emails and all other analysts must see "REDACTED". The team wants no second copy of the data. What should they create?

choices.text: A dynamic view that uses is_account_group_member() in a CASE expression on the email column
A streaming table that reads the emails and replaces them on each refresh with a mask
A materialized view per group, each storing its own copy of the table with masked values
A temporary view, because it applies each user's access rules for every workspace

stem: What is the key difference between a dynamic view and a materialized view in Databricks SQL?

choices.text: A dynamic view requires a streaming source; a materialized view requires an external database
A dynamic view computes at query time, varying by user; a materialized view stores precomputed results
A dynamic view stores its result and refreshes it; a materialized view recalculates the query on each read
A dynamic view can only be queried by its owner; a materialized view is readable by every workspace user

stem: A materialized view feeds a morning report. Upstream loads land at unpredictable times, and the team wants the view to update shortly after source data changes without keeping a fixed cron schedule. Which option fits?

choices.text: Convert the materialized view to a temporary view so that it is always current
Define the materialized view with a daily cron schedule at the earliest possible hour
Disable refreshes and run a full CREATE OR REPLACE by hand whenever someone remembers
Define the view with TRIGGER ON UPDATE so it refreshes when upstream source data changes

stem: An analyst builds a dynamic view that masks the email column for everyone outside the auditors group. A colleague outside that group still reads the full emails by querying the base table directly. What was missed?

choices.text: The colleague's session needs is_member() instead of is_account_group_member() for the mask to take effect
Dynamic views apply only to rows, so a column cannot be masked by any kind of view
The colleague can still read the base table, so that access must be removed and only the view granted
The view must be converted into a materialized view, because a standard view cannot hide columns

stem: An analyst runs CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW in the SQL editor on a SQL warehouse and later wants to know whether the latest refresh succeeded. What should the analyst know about how it runs?

choices.text: A serverless pipeline is created to process creation and refreshes, and status is visible in Catalog Explorer
Refreshes run on the analyst's laptop, so the status is found in the browser console
Refreshes run only when a dashboard opens, so no status is recorded anywhere for the view
The view is refreshed by a classic cluster that must be created and sized by the analyst

stem: Which statement correctly contrasts a standard view with a materialized view over the same large fact table?

choices.text: A standard view stores the query result; a materialized view runs the query again on every read
A standard view needs a streaming source; a materialized view needs an external catalog
A standard view computes results on demand; a materialized view stores the results and refreshes them
A standard view must be refreshed on a schedule; a materialized view never needs refreshing

stem: An analyst new to Databricks asks where the web application, notebook service and SQL editor backend run, compared with the place where a serverless SQL warehouse processes the data. Which description is correct?

choices.text: Both the web application and serverless compute run in the control plane, so they cannot read customer cloud storage
The web application runs in the control plane, and serverless compute runs in a serverless plane in the Databricks account
The web application runs in the customer's cloud account, and serverless compute runs in the classic compute plane inside the customer's virtual network
Both the web application and serverless compute run in the customer's cloud account, and Databricks only supplies the query engine software

stem: A retail company keeps sales history as files in cloud object storage. Analysts need reliable SQL queries with ACID transactions, while data scientists read the same data for ML. Which platform capability provides the transactional table layer on top of the files?

choices.text: Auto Loader, the file source that guarantees ACID behavior for every query that later reads the files it ingested
Catalog Explorer, the browser that maintains a lock file next to each dataset so analysts never read half-written files
Photon, the vectorized query engine that stores each table in a proprietary format for transactional updates
Delta Lake, the open table format that adds a transaction log to Parquet files and gives consistent versions

stem: A team lead asks which Databricks component an analyst uses to run SQL queries and build dashboards against lakehouse data without managing clusters, as opposed to the component data engineers use to build ingestion and transformation pipelines. Which pairing is correct?

choices.text: Analysts use Mosaic AI to run SQL queries; data engineers use Unity Catalog to transform and load the data into tables
Analysts use Lakeflow Jobs to run ad hoc queries; data engineers use Databricks SQL to schedule and orchestrate their pipelines
Analysts use Lakebase to build dashboards; data engineers use Delta Sharing to run scheduled transformations in notebooks
Analysts use Databricks SQL with SQL warehouses; data engineers use Lakeflow for ingestion, pipelines and jobs

stem: A product team needs a low-latency transactional backend for an internal app that records order status updates, and it wants the lakehouse tables in Unity Catalog available to the same app with Postgres queries. Which Databricks component fits?

choices.text: A serverless SQL warehouse, because it is optimized for many small single-row transactions issued by application users
Lakebase, the managed Postgres database that can sync Unity Catalog tables for low-latency app reads
A Lakeflow Declarative Pipeline, because it hosts the Postgres endpoints applications connect to
A Databricks Marketplace listing, because installing it turns a Delta table into a row-store with millisecond updates

stem: A company runs a workspace for finance analysts and a second workspace for marketing analysts in the same cloud region, both attached to the same Unity Catalog metastore. A marketing analyst who was granted SELECT on `finance.reports.q3_summary` opens the marketing workspace. What does the analyst see?

choices.text: The same table, because the metastore holds the metadata and permissions that every attached workspace shares
A read-only snapshot taken when the analyst was granted access, which is not refreshed afterwards
The table only after a workspace admin recreates the grant separately inside the marketing workspace
Nothing, because each workspace keeps its own catalogs and the table must be copied into the marketing workspace

stem: Analysts want to ask questions such as "which region had the highest revenue last quarter?" in plain English and get answers from governed tables, without writing SQL. Which platform component is designed for this?

choices.text: A materialized view that stores the answers to every possible question and refreshes them each night
A Lakeflow Connect connector that rewrites business questions into ingestion queries on the source systems, then loads the answer
An AI/BI Genie agent (Genie space) that translates natural language questions into SQL over the datasets it was configured with
A Photon-enabled warehouse, which interprets English text natively once the table comments are filled in

stem: A manager asks why the company stores data in the lakehouse instead of keeping a separate data warehouse for BI and a data lake for data science. Which reason reflects the lakehouse design?

choices.text: The lakehouse duplicates every table into a proprietary warehouse format so that BI queries never touch the files in the data lake
The lakehouse supports only unstructured data, so tabular reporting must stay in a separate warehouse product
The lakehouse removes the need for access control, because open file formats cannot hold sensitive data
One copy of data in open formats on cloud storage serves SQL analytics, BI and ML, with a table layer that adds transactions and governance

stem: Data engineers need to continuously load records from a SaaS application into the lakehouse without writing code, and analysts will then query the resulting tables in Databricks SQL. Which Databricks component handles the loading?

choices.text: Lakeflow Connect, which provides managed connectors to enterprise applications, databases and other sources
Catalog Explorer lineage, which pulls rows from the SaaS application whenever someone opens the lineage tab
Genie Code, which creates the source connection by interpreting the application's web page in the editor
AI/BI dashboards, which ingest the application data into Delta tables when a dataset is added to a page

stem: A marketing analyst wants to call a hosted language model from a SQL query to classify customer reviews as positive or negative, without leaving Databricks SQL. What makes this possible?

choices.text: Predictive Optimization, which rewrites a SQL query to include a sentiment model when the column is text
Delta time travel, which lets a query read a model version through a VERSION AS OF clause
AI Functions, SQL functions that give analysts access to AI models directly within queries and pipelines
A metric view, which stores the classification model as a measure for dashboards to apply

stem: Data engineers describe a Lakeflow pipeline as "declarative". What does this mean for the datasets, such as materialized views and streaming tables, that analysts later query?

choices.text: The engineers must write the refresh order of every dataset by hand, and the pipeline only runs the steps one by one
The engineers define the target datasets and their queries, and the pipeline works out the dependencies and run order
The datasets are defined in a dashboard, and the pipeline copies them into each analyst's personal schema
The pipeline stores only query text and evaluates it again for every analyst who reads one of its datasets

stem: An analyst sees the table reference `sales.emea.orders` in a query. Which reading of the three-level name is correct?

choices.text: Workspace `sales`, catalog `emea`, table `orders`
Metastore `sales`, schema `emea`, view `orders`
Catalog `sales`, schema `emea`, table `orders`
Schema `sales`, table `emea`, column `orders`

stem: Data scientists drop PDF contracts, images and CSV extracts into a shared location. Analysts need these files governed by the same Unity Catalog permissions as tables, addressed with a catalog.schema name, although the files are not rows and columns. Which object fits?

choices.text: A temporary view over the folder, which grants access to every file in the notebook that created it
A SQL warehouse, which stores the files and applies table privileges to them
A materialized view, which converts each file into a row and refreshes it daily
A Unity Catalog volume, which governs non-tabular files of any format

stem: An analyst gets a table with salary, home address and several business columns. Sales managers need only the business columns, and the team wants them to query a governed object without being granted SELECT on the table itself. What fits?

choices.text: A table comment that tells the managers which columns they should not query, since comments restrict columns
A view that selects only the business columns, with SELECT granted on the view and not on the base table
A copy of the table in a new schema that keeps every column, with the salary column renamed
A temporary view created in the analyst's notebook, which the managers can open from their own sessions

stem: Three dashboards each define "revenue per distinct customer" slightly differently, and the figures do not match. The team wants one governed definition that every dashboard, notebook and Genie agent reuses while allowing grouping by any field. What should they create?

choices.text: A Unity Catalog metric view that defines the measure once and lets users group by any dimension
An external table that stores a precomputed revenue-per-customer column for the most common grouping
A standard view that holds the revenue-per-customer value already computed for one fixed grouping, per region
A temporary view in each notebook with the same SQL pasted so that all copies remain identical

stem: A data steward wants analysts to recognize at a glance which gold tables meet the organization's quality standards and which old tables should no longer be used. Which Unity Catalog feature supports this?

choices.text: A SQL warehouse tag that marks all queries run from the warehouse as trusted for dashboards
A workspace folder named "approved" into which the stewards copy the tables that meet the standard each quarter
A table comment that analysts must read, because comments change the privileges of the table
The `system.certification_status` system tag with the values `certified` and `deprecated`

stem: Before renaming a column in `silver.orders`, an analyst wants to know which downstream tables, jobs and dashboards use it. Where can this be checked without reading any code?

choices.text: In the table's DESCRIBE HISTORY output, which names the dashboards that read the table
In Catalog Explorer on the table's Lineage tab, which shows upstream and downstream dependencies by column
In the SQL warehouse settings page, which lists every query that referenced the table over the last year of use
In the Marketplace provider console, which records the consumers of every Unity Catalog table

stem: A table was created in a notebook as `CREATE TEMPORARY VIEW recent_orders AS SELECT ...`. A colleague cannot find `recent_orders` in Catalog Explorer and gets "table or view not found" in her own notebook. Why?

choices.text: A temporary view is scoped to the session or query that created it and is not registered in any schema or catalog
Temporary views are registered in the metastore but are visible only after the workspace admin certifies them
The view was dropped automatically because Unity Catalog allows views only inside the default catalog
Views cannot be shared between users, so every analyst must recreate the view in a separate workspace

stem: A table in the `finance` catalog is queried with `SELECT * FROM delta.`s3://bucket/path``, referencing storage by path. Compared with querying it by table name, what is the effect on lineage?

choices.text: Lineage becomes more detailed, because the path lets Unity Catalog read the individual files and columns directly
Lineage is captured identically, because both forms are resolved to the same registered table
Catalog Explorer shows no column lineage, because it needs both source and target referenced by table name
Lineage is captured only for the first run of the query and is reset after the cluster restarts

stem: An analyst needs to explore which datasets exist, read column descriptions and sample the data of a table before writing a query. Which tool is the intended place to do this?

choices.text: The job run page of Lakeflow Jobs, which shows a preview of every table touched by the task
The Spark UI of a running cluster, which lists the tables of the metastore and their column comments
The Delta transaction log folder, which must be opened in cloud storage to read the schema and sample rows
Catalog Explorer, the UI for discovering and managing data and AI assets registered in Unity Catalog

stem: Which statement about the word "managed" for Unity Catalog tables is correct?

choices.text: A managed table is the only kind of table that Unity Catalog governs; external tables are outside access control and auditing
Unity Catalog controls the storage location and file lifecycle of a managed table, and external tables are still governed
A managed table is stored in the Databricks account, which means the company no longer owns the data files
It is a table whose owner holds the MANAGE privilege, which decides where the files are stored

stem: A sales analyst wants to find a ready-made third-party dataset that can be queried next to company tables in Unity Catalog. Which Databricks capability is built for this?

choices.text: Databricks Marketplace, an open exchange where providers publish datasets, notebooks and AI models for consumers
Lakeflow Jobs, a scheduler that publishes the company's tables to external buyers on a cron schedule
SQL alerts, a notification feature that emails analysts whenever a new public dataset appears
Genie Code, an assistant that finds and downloads open datasets from the internet when asked in natural language, then registers them as tables

stem: An analyst has no Databricks workspace yet but wants to look at what data products are listed before the company decides to adopt the platform. What is possible?

choices.text: Nothing yet, because listings are visible only to workspace admins after they install a provider connector
Browse listings only after a provider approves the analyst's email, since all listings are private exchanges
Browse the Open Marketplace, which needs no workspace; requesting access needs the Marketplace in a workspace
Request and receive any listing from the Open Marketplace without an account, because it needs no sign-in

stem: A consumer installs a free sample dataset listed on Databricks Marketplace into a Unity Catalog workspace. How do analysts typically work with it?

choices.text: It is exposed as a Lakebase database, and queries must use Postgres drivers outside of the SQL editor
It is copied into a managed table owned by the analyst, and the provider loses access to the data
It appears as a read-only catalog in Unity Catalog that analysts query with SQL and join to their own tables
It is attached to the workspace as a notebook only, because Marketplace shares code and never tables

stem: A company wants to try a partner BI tool with its lakehouse data and have the required Databricks resources set up automatically. Which feature is meant, and how does it differ from Marketplace?

choices.text: Partner Connect is a data sharing protocol that exposes tables to external tools, while Marketplace is the SQL editor tab for partner queries
Both are the same feature, and Partner Connect is the former name of Marketplace listings for datasets
Marketplace sets up partner trial accounts and connects them to the workspace; Partner Connect is an exchange of listings
Partner Connect sets up partner trial accounts and connects them to the workspace; Marketplace is an exchange of listings

stem: A provider offers a dataset that only members of a partner network should see, and a request must be approved before access is granted. Which Marketplace arrangement matches?

choices.text: A private exchange listing shared with member consumers, with provider approval of requests
A workspace folder share, in which the provider grants Can View on a notebook folder in its workspace
An external table registered by the partner in the provider's metastore, readable by any workspace in the region
A public listing with instant access, which every consumer can request and receive immediately

stem: An analyst opens the performance insights of a slow report query. One insight needs a change to the SQL text, and another needs a layout change on a table. The analyst selects Optimize next to the insights. What does Genie Code do?

choices.text: It opens the documentation page of each insight and lists the links, because it can neither edit SQL statements nor summarize recommended actions
It rewrites the query for insights that need a query change and presents the changes for approval, and it summarizes table or compute changes as plain text
It applies every recommendation straight to the query, the tables and the warehouse, without asking for approval, and reports afterwards what it changed
It rewrites the query for insights that need a query change, and then silently runs `OPTIMIZE` on the tables and resizes the warehouse on its own

stem: A dashboard query that used to finish in seconds now takes minutes. An analyst opens the query's details from query history and wants to see which individual steps of the execution consumed the most time, without reading the whole plan graph. Which part of the query profile helps most?

choices.text: The Details panel, which shows only the status and the user who started the query run
The Query text panel, which lists the full SQL statement along with the warehouse and the user that executed it earlier
The query source link, which opens the dashboard dataset and shows its last edit time and author
The Top operators panel, which lists the longest running operators so costly steps stand out

stem: The Performance insights tab of a dashboard query shows `SHORT_QUERY_PRIORITIZATION` with the label Accelerated and no other insight. What does this tell the analyst?

choices.text: Databricks predicted that the query would be short and ran it at once through a fast path although the cluster was at capacity, so no action is needed
Databricks flagged the query as short but held it in the queue until capacity was free, so the analyst should split the dataset into several queries
Databricks found that the query spilled to disk while running at capacity, so the analyst should select a larger warehouse size for this query
Databricks found the query too heavy for the warehouse and queued it behind lighter queries, so the analyst should raise the maximum number of clusters

stem: In the query details panel, a query shows a wall-clock duration of 40 seconds and an aggregated task time of 6 minutes. What does the aggregated task time represent?

choices.text: The time the query waited in the warehouse queue before any compute resources were assigned to it
The combined execution time across all cores of all nodes, which can exceed wall-clock time
The time spent reading the final result back from cloud storage into the SQL editor session after the run
The time the optimizer needed to plan the query and to prune files before the execution started

stem: A dashboard dataset is defined as `SELECT * FROM sales.fact_orders`, and the dashboard shows only four of the 60 columns. The query's performance insights list `WIDE_PROJECTION`. What does the insight recommend?

choices.text: Run `VACUUM` on the fact table, because the insight is about unused columns that are still stored in the table files
Add a `LIMIT` clause to the dataset query, because the insight is about the number of rows that the query returns
Select only the needed columns in the dataset query instead of all columns, which reduces the bytes read by the scan
Increase the maximum number of clusters, because the insight is about the 60 columns being spread over too few clusters

stem: A query on a table made of thousands of tiny files is slow, and its profile shows a `DATA_FILE_SIZE` insight. The table is a Unity Catalog managed table partitioned by date. Which recommendation set matches the insight?

choices.text: Enable predictive optimization or run `OPTIMIZE` to compact files, and consider liquid clustering for partitioned tables
Run `VACUUM` with a zero-hour retention so that all small files disappear from the table immediately
Disable the disk cache on the warehouse, because small files only appear when cached copies are never evicted from local storage
Convert the managed table into an external table so that the cloud store merges small files by itself

stem: An analyst wants a colleague to review the query profile of a slow query. The colleague is a workspace member, but has no CAN MANAGE permission on the query. How can the analyst share the profile?

choices.text: Select Share and send the copied URL, which opens the profile for every workspace member, whatever permission they hold on the query
Download the profile as a JSON file, which the colleague imports into their own session with Import query profile (JSON) in query history
Export the query result as a CSV file, because the colleague can rebuild the profile from the returned rows when importing the file
Grant the colleague CAN USE on the SQL warehouse, which is enough for opening the profiles of all queries that ran on it

stem: An auditor asks which user last changed the `finance.ledger` Delta table, when, and with what kind of operation (for example MERGE or DELETE). Which command returns this information?

choices.text: `DESCRIBE DETAIL finance.ledger`, because it returns the audit trail with one row for each write operation
`SHOW TBLPROPERTIES finance.ledger`, because it keeps a log of each user who modified the table
`SELECT * FROM finance.ledger VERSION AS OF 0`, because it lists the users who edited the table in the past
`DESCRIBE HISTORY finance.ledger`, which returns the operation, user and timestamp of each write, newest first

stem: A monthly revenue figure changed between Monday's board report and Tuesday's. The analyst needs to compare the `sales_summary` Delta table as of Monday's last commit with its current state to find the rows that differ. What is the right approach?

choices.text: Clone the table with `CREATE TABLE ... DEEP CLONE` after the change so that the older rows are available for comparison
Run `RESTORE TABLE sales_summary` to Monday's version, query it, then restore forward again to the latest one
Read Monday's state with `VERSION AS OF` or `TIMESTAMP AS OF` and compare it with the current table using `EXCEPT`
Ask the data engineers to rebuild the table from the source system and compare the rebuilt copy to the current table

stem: In `DESCRIBE HISTORY`, an analyst sees many `OPTIMIZE` rows for a table and wants to know which ones were started by a person or a scheduled job and which were automatic compaction after writes. Which column separates them?

choices.text: `operationParameters`, where `auto` is `true` for automatic compaction and `false` for a command run by a user or a scheduled job
`operation`, which reads `OPTIMIZE AUTO` for automatic compaction and `OPTIMIZE MANUAL` for runs started by a person or a job
`readVersion`, which stays empty for automatic compaction because that kind of run never reads an earlier table version
`userMetadata`, which holds the word AUTO for each compaction triggered by a write and stays empty for every manual run

stem: A query shows a `CONCURRENT_WRITE` insight, because writes to the table conflicted. The analyst wants to find which writes overlapped. Which recommendation and source fit the insight?

choices.text: Increase the warehouse size so that every writer gets more memory, because write conflicts appear when writers run out of memory
Select only the needed columns in the writing queries, because wide projections make concurrent writers collide on commits
Review the Delta table history to identify the concurrent writes, then adjust the scheduling of the jobs so they stop overlapping
Collect Delta statistics with `ANALYZE`, because missing statistics are what makes two writers conflict on the same table

stem: After a data fix, an analyst wants to confirm that the nightly MERGE actually touched the expected number of rows. Where does the evidence sit in the table history?

choices.text: In the `userName` column, which lists how many rows each user has changed in total
In the `operationMetrics` column of the MERGE row, which reports rows inserted, updated and deleted
In the `readVersion` column, which counts the rows read by the MERGE
In the `isolationLevel` column, which records how many rows were affected by each operation in total

stem: An analyst remembers running a complex join query last week but cannot find it in the editor. A teammate also needs to find all queries that ran on a specific SQL warehouse and took more than a minute. Which feature covers both needs?

choices.text: The Delta table history of the queried tables, which lists the SELECT statements of each user
The disk cache of the cluster, which keeps a list of recently scanned files and the queries behind them
The result cache of the SQL warehouse, which lists the earlier statements together with their results
Query history, which can be filtered by user, date range, compute, duration, status and statement type

stem: A BI user reruns the same aggregate query on a SQL warehouse several times in a row. The underlying tables have not changed. The second and third runs return almost instantly. Which mechanism explains this?

choices.text: Liquid clustering, which rewrites the table after the first run so repeated queries skip the work
Photon, which permanently stores the output of every aggregate query that it has ever run
Result caching, which returns the stored result of an identical query while the tables are unchanged
The Delta transaction log, which stores the aggregated results of every query with each table version

stem: A pro SQL warehouse is stopped every night by its auto stop setting. Each morning, the first execution of a heavy dashboard query is slow, while reruns later in the day are fast. A colleague says the cache is why. What does the warehouse lose when it stops?

choices.text: The local result cache and the disk cache, which are cleared on stop or restart and must be repopulated
The Delta table data files, which are removed from storage when the warehouse stops
The access permissions on the tables, which have to be granted again by an owner after each warehouse start
The query history entries and query profiles, which are deleted whenever the warehouse stops

stem: An analyst compares two versions of a query to see if a rewrite is faster. Re-running the original query returns instantly because of caching, which makes the timing comparison meaningless. What should the analyst do while testing?

choices.text: Run `OPTIMIZE` on the table before every timing so that the caches are cleared by the compaction step
Run `SET use_cached_result = false` in the SQL editor for the test session only
Switch the table from managed to external so that results are no longer cached
Delete the query from query history so that the engine forgets its earlier result

stem: A team uses an AI/BI dashboard and a saved SQL query in the SQL editor, and wonders why a cached result seems to apply differently. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: The Databricks SQL UI cache applies to AI/BI dashboards as well, and has the same 7-day life cycle everywhere
Neither feature caches anything, because only notebooks use query caches in Databricks
Both use only the disk cache, so results are never stored and each viewer always recomputes everything
AI/BI dashboards have their own caching behavior, and the Databricks SQL UI cache does not apply to them

stem: Which operations does predictive optimization run automatically on Unity Catalog managed tables?

choices.text: `OPTIMIZE`, `VACUUM` and `ANALYZE`, run only on tables that would benefit, as determined by Databricks
`RESTORE`, `CLONE` and `COPY INTO`, run after each failed job to recover earlier versions of tables
`CREATE VIEW`, `GRANT` and `REFRESH`, run whenever a user opens a table in Catalog Explorer
`MERGE`, `UPDATE` and `DELETE`, run on every table each night so that data stays fresh

stem: Predictive optimization was enabled explicitly for the `sales` catalog. Later an account admin disables the account-level setting to cut cost. What happens to the `sales` catalog?

choices.text: It is disabled only for tables created after the change, because existing tables keep the setting they had at creation time
It is disabled too, because the account setting always overrides every explicit choice made at a lower level of the hierarchy
It stays enabled, because disabling at the account level does not disable catalogs or schemas that explicitly enabled the feature
It is paused until the catalog owner confirms the change, because the account setting cannot change a lower level on its own

stem: A managed table used to be partitioned by `event_date`, but analysts now filter mostly by `customer_id` or `region`, and these patterns keep shifting. The team wants the data layout to adapt automatically. Which statement fits?

choices.text: `ALTER TABLE events ADD PARTITION (customer_id)` for each customer, so every future filter is covered
`OPTIMIZE events ZORDER BY (event_date)` once a week, which then adapts to the changing filter columns
`ALTER TABLE events SET TBLPROPERTIES ('layout' = 'automatic')`, which makes the table adapt itself
`ALTER TABLE events REPLACE PARTITIONED BY WITH CLUSTER BY AUTO`, so clustering keys follow query patterns

stem: A table has `CLUSTER BY AUTO` enabled, but several weeks later no clustering keys have been chosen. An analyst wants to see why. According to the documentation, which explanation is possible?

choices.text: Keys are only chosen for tables with an `ORDER BY` clause in each query, and the analysts do not use it
The table is too small, already has an effective layout, or has few queries, so selection did not pay off
Clustering keys can only be chosen on the first day after the table is created, and that time has passed
Automatic liquid clustering is disabled for any table with several analysts, so no keys are chosen

stem: A data analyst who owns no objects but has `SELECT` and `MODIFY` on a managed table asks for predictive optimization to be turned off for that table. Who can change the setting for the table?

choices.text: Any user with `MODIFY` on the table, since changing the setting counts as a write to the table
Only an account admin, because the setting exists at the account level alone and tables just inherit it
Any user with `SELECT` on the table, because the setting changes only how the table is read
The table owner, or a user with the `MANAGE` privilege on the table

stem: A data owner wants to know which tables predictive optimization has processed, what it ran, and what it cost. Where does Databricks provide this?

choices.text: In the query profile of any dashboard query, which shows maintenance totals for the whole schema and catalog
In the `system.query.history` table, which lists each maintenance run as a separate SELECT statement
In `system.storage.predictive_optimization_operations_history`, which records operations, costs and impact
In the result cache of the warehouse, which stores a summary of every maintenance run

stem: An analyst's queries on an external Delta table that was manually optimized with `OPTIMIZE ... ZORDER BY` show a `MANUAL_DATA_LAYOUT` insight. What does the insight recommend?

choices.text: Rewrite every query with a hint, because the insight is about the optimizer ignoring manual layout
Convert to managed, enable predictive optimization and automatic liquid clustering to reduce bytes read
Delete the Z-order and keep the table as it is, because manual layouts always outperform the automatic ones
Move the table to a smaller SQL warehouse, because manual layouts only work on small compute

stem: A managed table's access pattern changes: for years most queries filtered on `store_id`, but since a reporting change, most filter on `product_category`. The table uses automatic liquid clustering. What happens, according to how the feature works?

choices.text: Databricks can select new keys, but only when the predicted data skipping savings outweigh the cost of reclustering
Nothing changes until an engineer redefines the clustering keys manually, because keys are fixed after the first selection
Keys switch immediately after the first query on the new column, regardless of the cost of reclustering the table
The table is deleted and recreated each time the pattern changes, so queries fail until the new layout is ready
